Old Native American tale… or thats how it was told to me..

An Indian climbed to the top of a mountain top to survey the land. The Indian replied "But you are a rattle snake, you will surely bite me"… The rattle snake replied "I promise I will not bite you because you are being kind and helping me". The Shah of Kwharezm and the Prince From the East.

Long ago, there was a mighty Empire in the Middle East, ruled by the Shah of Khwarezm. His empire was about the size of the Persian empire, and he had everything a man at that time could ask for.

One day, the Shah receives a message, from an emissary in the service of a young Prince from the East. The Prince wishes to establish trade relations between the two leaders, and to one day re-open the Silk Road.

The Shah dismisses this offer, as there was no equal to his regal might, so he has the emissary executed. Now, the Prince from the East was a patient man, and thought there must have been some kind of mistake for his emissary to be executed, so he sent a second envoy, this time with caravans full of jewels, precious metals, spices and concubines.

After receiving this envoy, the Shah was even more offended, this time by the notion that his nation could be bought by trinkets and whores, and so the concubines were executed, the spices dumped at sea, the jewels smashed to dust, and the precious metals were melted down and poured in the eyes and ears of the envoy and his guards.

The Prince from the East was not happy with this recent turn of events, for his name was Genghis Khan, and this offensive refusal made him so angry that he sent his army to this great empire, broke the back of its army by outnumbering them 5-1, executed and enslaved all of the remaining citizens, and burned the capital of Samarkand to the ground. The Shah of Khwarezm died alone, on the streets of his once great empire.

Never underestimate your enemy. His wrath could match that of Genghis Khan.
